tiers.label: Core
tiers.description: The complete local worldbuilding toolset, free for good.

tiers.label: Apprentice+
tiers.description: Monthly Mimir AI credits, desktop and phone sync, and one hosted Campaign.

tiers.label: Worldsmith+
tiers.description: Lore review, the Writers' Room, Export to Engine and bigger Campaigns.

tiers.label: Loremaster
tiers.description: Proving Grounds, the largest allowances and priority support.

categories.label: Build
categories.title: Give every idea room to become a world.
categories.purpose: Create and structure the world's information without turning creativity into form-filling.
categories.intro: Start with a name and a thought. Add fields, links, imagery and structure only when the world needs them.

features.name: Structured world entries
features.summary: Create characters, species, cultures, places, factions, artefacts, events, languages, spells and other connected lore.
features.detail: Mimir gives common world entities purpose-built structure while keeping the minimum required information deliberately small.
features.imageAlt: Óðinn's character entry in Mimir: portrait, name and aliases, structured frontmatter such as species, culture and birthplace, his class paths, and calculated stats.
features.mediaCaption: A character entry with structured fields, class paths and stats.

features.name: Flexible entry editors
features.summary: Begin with as little as you know, then deepen an entry as the idea grows.
features.detail: Shared fields such as aliases, worlds, spoilers, tags and images sit alongside type-specific details. Empty optional fields do not become creative homework.

features.name: Entry type editor
features.summary: Make your own entry types and fields, or change the built-in ones, to fit your world.
features.detail: Choose from 15 kinds of field, save an entry type as your personal default, and keep sets of entry types as presets you can apply to any world or share as a file.

features.name: Random tables
features.summary: Roll on weighted tables you write, or pick a random entry from your own world.
features.detail: Random tables live in the sidebar roller. Its "Your entries" tab draws from a filtered set of your own entries, using the same filters as the Browser. Nothing is invented: every result comes from your world.

features.name: Assets & media
features.summary: Keep images and supporting media connected to the entries that use them.
features.detail: Assets own their file, alt text and licence metadata, making reuse and attribution more deliberate across a world.

features.name: Hero images
features.summary: Choose one reusable lead image for an entry, browser card or narrative beat.
features.detail: Hero images are references to managed Assets rather than duplicate uploads. Galleries can coexist with the lead image.
features.media: Hero image across editor and Browser
features.imageAlt: The Mimir library grid, where each entry shows its hero image.

features.name: Random names from your lists
features.summary: Give a culture its own name lists, then press Random name on a character.
features.detail: Mimir picks names only from lists you wrote. It uses no AI, costs nothing and works offline.

features.name: Game-system templates
features.summary: Start a world with the Default entry types or the free D&D 5e (SRD 5.2) template.
features.detail: Templates are built in and free, chosen when you make a world and changeable in Settings. Content packs for them are sold separately. Mimir is not affiliated with or endorsed by Wizards of the Coast.

categories.label: Connect
categories.title: Turn pages into a living system.
categories.purpose: Reveal how people, places, cultures, histories and ideas depend on one another.
categories.intro: A world is defined by the relationships between its pieces, not merely by the existence of pages.

features.name: Links
features.summary: Reference another entry naturally while writing and move straight to its context.
features.detail: Type [[ and a name to link another entry while you write. Links make connected lore part of the writing flow instead of a separate database chore.

features.name: Backlinks
features.summary: See every place that refers back to an entry.
features.detail: Backlinks expose the consequences and context surrounding an entity, including narrative-planning references where supported.
features.imageAlt: The Appears in section of Fenrir's entry, listing Angrboða, Binding Spells and Gleipnir, each with the passage that mentions him and its links highlighted.
features.mediaCaption: Backlinks with context: every entry that mentions Fenrir, and what it says.

features.name: Relationships & inverse links
features.summary: Model explicit, typed connections between entries rather than relying on prose alone.
features.detail: Relationships are typed, can carry a score and can be one-sided. See them on an entry, in a matrix, and in the Relationships and World Connections graphs.
features.imageAlt: Mimir's Relationships graph: typed bonds between characters, cultures and factions, with filters by relationship type.

features.name: Tags & linked navigation
features.summary: Group ideas across entity types and follow connections without losing your place.
features.detail: Tags, worlds and linked entities give multiple ways to move through the same canon depending on the question being asked.

categories.label: Visualise
categories.title: See structures prose cannot hold.
categories.purpose: Expose lineage, hierarchy, geography and chronology as visual systems.
categories.intro: Mimir does not flatten every connection into one generic graph. Each view is designed around the structure it needs to explain.

features.name: Family Tree
features.summary: Trace ancestry, partners and family lines through a focused genealogy view.
features.detail: Family structure is presented as genealogy rather than a generic relationship diagram, with filters for large worlds.
features.imageAlt: Mimir's family tree for Óðinn and Frigg, with their children, the spouses Nanna and Sif, and Baldr's son Forseti.

features.name: Genus / Species Tree
features.summary: Understand taxonomic branches and how species relate across a world.
features.detail: The genus view supports its own hierarchy and filtering, including habitat and diet dimensions documented by the application.
features.imageAlt: Mimir's species tree: Giants at the root, with the Æsir Gods, Dwarves, Monsters, Norns and Vanir Gods below and the Einherjar, Valkyrie-Kin and Elves further down.

features.name: Culture Tree
features.summary: Explore parent, descendant and related cultural structures.
features.detail: Culture hierarchy can focus on a selected branch or expand to a wider view of the world's cultural structure.
features.imageAlt: Mimir's culture tree: Proto-Norse branching into the Æsir, Jötnar and Vanir, with the Berserkers, Skalds and Álfar below.

features.name: Faction Tree
features.summary: Arrange members, roles and internal connections as an organisation actually works.
features.detail: Faction trees support free-form member structure, roles and decorative connections rather than forcing every organisation into a strict hierarchy.

features.name: Place Tree
features.summary: Move from worlds and regions down through settlements and contained places.
features.detail: The place hierarchy makes containment and scale visible, with focused and wider views for large settings.

features.name: Advanced tree filtering
features.summary: Narrow each specialised tree with filters that match its subject.
features.detail: Family, genus, place, culture and faction trees each have filters that suit them, and Mimir remembers your choices.

features.name: Timeline
features.summary: Understand events across the world's chronology instead of reconstructing order from pages.
features.detail: Timeline views place connected events against the active calendar and world context.
features.imageAlt: The timeline of the Mythic Age with the event Surtr's Burning opened.

features.name: Calendar
features.summary: Define in-world time and use it consistently across events and planning.
features.detail: Calendars provide the chronology that events, timelines and narrative work can share.

features.name: Interactive maps
features.summary: Connect locations and entries to geography rather than keeping place trapped in prose.
features.detail: A map is an entry built on your own picture, with pins that link to the entries they mark. Pinned entries show where they appear on a map.
features.imageAlt: The Nine Realms map with the Jötunheim pin selected and its linked entry shown.

categories.label: Write & Plan
categories.title: Use the world while shaping what happens in it.
categories.purpose: Develop stories, campaigns and interactive narratives beside the lore they depend on.
categories.intro: These are narrative and world-use tools inside Mimir's connected platform, not an attempt to turn it into a generic novel-writing app.

features.name: Story Arc editor
features.summary: Structure an arc and connect its people, events and places back to canon.
features.detail: Story arcs are first-class world entries, so planning can remain connected to the wider world instead of becoming an isolated outline.

features.name: Narrative Planner
features.summary: Arrange visual beats, branches and connected lore across a wider narrative canvas.
features.detail: Lay out beats as boxes, join them with labelled lines and write what happens. When the shape feels right, turn beats and their links into real entries.
features.imageAlt: The Road to Ragnarök in Mimir's Narrative Planner: six illustrated beats from The Grievances Gather to The Doom Falls, joined by labelled edges, with one beat open in the inspector.
features.mediaCaption: A story planned as illustrated beats with labelled consequences.

features.name: Quest Editor
features.summary: Design objectives, consequences and connected lore for interactive stories or campaigns.
features.detail: Quests are graphs of objectives, choices, conditions and consequences, and can be stepped through in Simulation on every plan.
features.imageAlt: The quest graph for The Binding of Fenrir, branching at a choice into two outcomes.

features.name: Dialogue Editor
features.summary: Build branching conversations with the characters and context they reference.
features.detail: Dialogue is a connected creative tool rather than a detached script file, and you can test it in Simulation.
features.imageAlt: The dialogue Þórr and the Ferryman as a graph of lines and a choice, during a test run.

features.name: Spoiler-aware planning
features.summary: Keep reveals and secret information controlled while using lore in plans.
features.detail: Spoiler metadata follows entries into connected planning and export workflows so different audiences can receive appropriate context.

categories.label: Understand
categories.title: Find answers. Catch problems. Keep canon grounded.
categories.purpose: Retrieve the right information and distinguish structural certainty from language-based review.
categories.intro: Search, deterministic validation and AI review work together, but they do not pretend to be the same kind of evidence.

features.name: Browser, search & filters
features.summary: Find entries with fuzzy search and combine filters for type, world, spoiler level and tags.
features.detail: The Browser is a working surface for navigating large worlds, not merely a list of recent documents.
features.imageAlt: The Mimir workspace: the sidebar with world and library navigation, and the library grid of illustrated entries with filters by type.
features.mediaCaption: The workspace and library, filtered by entry type.

features.name: Deterministic validation
features.summary: Catch known structural problems using rules whose results can be explained.
features.detail: Validation checks explicit data constraints and reference integrity. It does not use probabilistic language interpretation.

features.name: Naming consistency
features.summary: Surface likely naming clashes before they spread through a connected world.
features.detail: Naming checks support deliberate reuse while helping creators notice accidental collisions and confusing near-matches.

features.name: Mimir AI
features.summary: Ask grounded questions using relevant world context without silently declaring inventions canon.
features.detail: Ask questions in plain English. Mimir answers only from your world, cites the entries it used and says when the answer is not there. You can see exactly which entries it reads before it answers. It runs on Mimir Credits: every account gets a one-time welcome grant of 200 credits, and paid plans add a monthly allowance. These are planning figures and may change before checkout opens.
features.imageAlt: The What Mimir checks panel in Ask Mimir, showing the limits of what the AI reads, the reading depth, and the entries pinned for the conversation.
features.mediaCaption: Ask Mimir shows exactly which entries it reads.

features.name: Create entries with Ask Mimir
features.summary: Ask Mimir to make a minor character, item or place from what your world already holds.
features.detail: Mimir builds only from what your world already holds. If something it needs is missing, it says what to add first. The name comes from your own name lists. Nothing is saved until you confirm, and new entries are marked as needing follow-up.

features.name: Lore Consistency Review
features.summary: Review meaning-level contradictions that deterministic rules cannot understand alone.
features.detail: On Worldsmith and above, Mimir AI checks an entry, a group or the whole world for prose that contradicts its own details or another entry, and shows the evidence for each finding. It also checks your Rule entries against each other and the entries they govern. It uses credits and never rewrites your world.
features.imageAlt: The laws of the Nine Realms in the Loremaster, each with the number of entries it governs.

features.name: World briefs
features.summary: Package the right part of your world as one file for another AI tool.
features.detail: Choose all entries or a saved filter, a spoiler level and a world, edit the instructions the AI reads first, then copy it or save it. It runs on your computer and costs no credits. It is not a live MCP connection.
features.imageAlt: The World brief export, with scope, spoiler threshold and world filter settings.

features.name: Constructed-language (conlang) Translator
features.summary: Work with a world's own language using its documented vocabulary and rules.
features.detail: Write your language's rules in plain English and translate with Mimir AI. Any word Mimir has to invent is added to your vocabulary and listed, so you can regenerate or reject it. Words you keep are never swapped for synonyms. It uses Mimir Credits on every plan.

features.name: Voice dictation
features.summary: Speak instead of typing, on your own computer.
features.detail: Dictation uses a speech model you download once inside Mimir. After that it runs on your computer, works offline and costs no credits.

categories.label: Test
categories.title: Let the world move before it meets an audience.
categories.purpose: Explore dialogue, quests, choices and system behaviour while the work is still easy to change.
categories.intro: Simulation lets anyone step through quests and dialogue to find broken branches. Proving Grounds, on Loremaster, adds AI-refereed play against your world's rules.

features.name: Proving Grounds
features.summary: Play a game in your world with Mimir AI as the referee, against the Rule entries you wrote.
features.detail: Set the rules, the company and the game, then play turn by turn. Dice are rolled by the app and shown in the saga. You see the credit cost before you start. Every action, including creating, running, hosting and joining, needs Loremaster.
features.imageAlt: The Proving Grounds session setup screen in Mimir.

features.name: Dialogue testing
features.summary: Step through branching conversations and inspect how choices alter the exchange.
features.detail: Run a dialogue in Simulation, choose at each branch and watch variables change.
features.imageAlt: A dialogue test run paused where Þórr chooses how to answer the ferryman.

features.name: Quest testing
features.summary: Test objectives, outcomes and dependencies before using them in a live story or campaign.
features.detail: Run a quest in Simulation from a fresh state or a saved preset, then see the outcome and which parts were never reached.
features.imageAlt: A finished quest test run with its outcome and coverage of reached and unreached nodes.

features.name: Variables & world state
features.summary: Represent facts that can change as choices and systems move the world forward.
features.detail: Declare the facts that can change (true or false, numbers, choices, entries, relationships), for the whole world or per character, faction or place. Quests and dialogue read and change them.
features.imageAlt: The Variables screen with typed world-state declarations used by quests and dialogue.

features.name: Simulation
features.summary: Explore how connected rules and changing state affect a designed world.
features.detail: Step through a quest or dialogue graph without a game engine, watch the state change, and save the run to share or test against later.
features.imageAlt: A simulation run reporting its outcome and which nodes it never reached.

features.name: Session & system prototyping
features.summary: Experiment with tabletop sessions and game rules in context, with Mimir AI as the referee.
features.detail: Part of Proving Grounds on Loremaster: define a game and play it against your world's rules.

categories.label: Own & Protect
categories.title: Local-first changes what you can rely on.
categories.purpose: Keep work readable, recoverable, portable and under creator control.
categories.intro: Local-first is not a privacy slogan. It means ordinary files remain accessible, worlds are not locked behind a subscription and history can help recover mistakes.

features.name: Local readable files
features.summary: Keep the core world on the creator's own machine in readable formats.
features.detail: Mimir's foundation is designed around creator-controlled local files rather than making a hosted account the only way to reach a world.
features.imageAlt: An entry open in Mimir beside the plain markdown file it is stored in.

features.name: Unlimited local worlds & entries
features.summary: Create locally without treating a creator's own files as a metered cloud resource.
features.detail: Core remains a substantial free local foundation, including unlimited local worlds and entries.

features.name: History and saved versions
features.summary: Review entry history and recover earlier work when an edit goes wrong.
features.detail: Turn history on and Mimir saves a version every time you save. Open any earlier version of an entry and restore it. Going back adds a new version, so nothing is lost.
features.imageAlt: An earlier version of Óðinn's entry opened from its history, showing the file as it was with a Restore this version button, above the list of past commits.
features.mediaCaption: Any past version of an entry can be opened and restored.

features.name: The Bin
features.summary: Everything you delete goes to the Bin first.
features.detail: Restore an entry exactly as it was. Deleting a whole world sends it to your computer's own recycle bin.

features.name: Standard export
features.summary: Take the world's material out in useful formats without a premium retrieval toll.
features.detail: Export a copy of your world as Markdown files or plain JSON on every plan. It runs on your computer.

features.name: Safe-to-publish export
features.summary: Prepare a public version that respects spoiler and reveal controls.
features.detail: Safe-to-publish export is distinct from World briefs: it is for audiences, not for sending a working context package to an AI tool.

features.name: Export to Engine
features.summary: Export your world for Unreal, Unity or Godot.
features.detail: Writes one JSON file per entry type, shaped for Unreal's DataTable import, Unity and Godot 4. It runs on your computer. It is a one-way export, not a live engine connection. Live engine integration, round-tripping and native engine formats come later.

features.name: Migration & general import
features.summary: Bring existing work into Mimir without paying extra to regain useful access to it.
features.detail: Turn CSV and XLSX spreadsheets into entries with a column-by-column mapping. Mimir AI can read TXT, Markdown and DOCX documents and suggest entries, with the evidence for each. Dedicated importers for an Obsidian vault, a Notion export or a World Anvil world use no AI and no credits. The World Anvil importer has been tested with sample exports. You review everything before anything is written.
features.imageAlt: Turning a spreadsheet into entries: each column matched to a field before anything is created.

features.name: Accessibility controls
features.summary: Adapt contrast, typography and reading behaviour to different needs.
features.detail: Mimir documents a dyslexia-first accessibility approach alongside keyboard navigation and reading controls.

features.name: Focus Mode
features.summary: Reduce interface noise when the work needs sustained attention.
features.detail: Focus Mode is part of the Core accessibility and writing environment rather than a premium productivity lock.

categories.label: Share
categories.title: Bring people into the world, not into a social feed.
categories.purpose: Collaborate, host and reveal the right information to the right people.
categories.intro: Mimir distinguishes collaborators who help shape the work from participants or players who experience a controlled view. It is not an open social network.

features.name: Spoiler controls
features.summary: Control what different audiences can see without maintaining separate copies of the world.
features.detail: Spoiler level and reveal metadata travel with entries into search, planning, hosting and safe-to-publish export.

features.name: Writers' Room
features.summary: Build one world together, with five roles from Owner to Viewer.
features.detail: Collaborators propose changes and the owner accepts them into their local canon. Creating or joining a Writers' Room needs Worldsmith, and every collaborator needs their own plan.
features.imageAlt: Joining a Writers' Room in Mimir: paste the invitation code the world's owner sent, with notes that the code alone decides which room you join and that nobody's world is copied to your computer.
features.mediaCaption: Joining a Writers' Room with the owner's invitation code. Every writer in the room needs Worldsmith.

features.name: Hosted worlds
features.summary: Make selected world access available beyond the local machine when hosting is needed.
features.detail: Host up to 5 Writers' Room worlds on Worldsmith or 20 on Loremaster, each with 5 or 20 guest collaborators. Your local copy stays the canon.

features.name: Host a Campaign
features.summary: Give players or participants a controlled experience without granting editor access.
features.detail: Players and Co-GMs see only what you give them. Apprentice hosts one Campaign for up to 8 people including you, with 1 GB and 1 live table. Worldsmith hosts several, for up to 20 people, with 3 GB and 2 live tables. Loremaster hosts several, for up to 50 people, with 10 GB and 5 live tables.
features.imageAlt: A preview of what one player can see, with everything withheld listed for the GM only.

features.name: Players join free
features.summary: Players and Co-GMs join a hosted Campaign on free Core.
features.detail: The host's plan covers the table. A Writers' Room is different: every writer needs Worldsmith.
features.imageAlt: What one player can see in a Campaign, with everything withheld listed for the GM only.

features.name: Run the session
features.summary: Track a fight, keep notes to hand and follow the in-world date.
features.detail: The encounter tracker keeps turn order, rounds, hit points and conditions, all typed by the GM, with no dice and no rules applied. The GM screen holds reference cards, pinned entries and timers. Each campaign keeps its own date on your world's calendar and its own quest progress.

features.name: Live collaborative Proving Grounds
features.summary: Host a live Proving Ground table and let other players join it.
features.detail: The host opens a live table and shares its live code. Up to eight players join, send the actions they want to take, and the host plays each turn. The host's Mimir runs the referee and spends the host's credits. Everyone at the table needs Loremaster.
features.media: Live Proving Grounds host and player views

features.name: Mimir on your phone
features.summary: Read and edit your worlds on your phone.
features.detail: The Mimir phone app keeps worlds on the phone, under your control. Some power-user screens, such as the Entry type editor, stay on the desktop.

features.name: Desktop and phone sync
features.summary: Keep your worlds in step between your computer and the Mimir phone app.
features.detail: Each sync is recorded as one step in your world's history, and anything Mimir cannot place is listed rather than dropped.

features.name: Content packs
features.summary: Optional Shieldwall packs of ready-made entries and art.
features.detail: Packs and collections are sold in Mimir's Marketplace, and paid checkout opens with the public beta. Packs start at £4.99. Collections are 20% off the packs you do not already own. Nothing in your world changes until you accept a pack update, and files a pack added stay on your disk.
